newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BIL calls for foreign media rules review.
newsitem.headline: BIL calls for foreign media rules review.

text.p: Brierley Investments Ltd (BIL) has again called for the Australian government to relax foreign ownership restrictions as part of its cross-media ownership review, a newspaper report published on Thursday said.
BIL executive director Rod Price told The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper it made no sense for the government not to review foreign ownership rules in the context of the cross-media ownership review.
"You can't just hog-tie one group to the rail and let one group run loose," Price was quoted as saying.
"It just doesn't make any sense and I can't believe they (the government) would be so narrow as to view it that way."
The New Zealand-based company is the largest shareholder in Australian newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd with a stake of 19.9 percent.

BIL is permitted to move to 25 percent over time under current foreign ownership policy, but the newspaper said it would lift its stake to 50 percent if the appropriate changes are made to media policy.

Price said the current mood in Canberra was to remove only the cross-media rules, but added that he believed foreign ownership changes would follow as politicians realised they would only get one chance to set media ownership policy.
"To do one without the other doesn't make sense and they will look like bunnies if they do it," Price said.
The Australian government has said in the past it was not inclined to allow increased foreign ownership of Australia's media.
Foreigners are currently limited to a 25 percent stake in newspapers and 15 percent in television companies.
Under current cross-media regulations, media proprietors are not allowed to control both broadcast and print media in the same market.
